# The second of the two Rosario confirmation registers that cover Pablo Armando's childhood; the Catedral was

*** THE FILM IS FINISHED - ALL 141 IMAGES, 14 September 2026 ***
column2: DGS 004581639, Santa Rosa de Lima, Rosario, Confirmaciones 1890-1897. Images 1-5 are covers. *** Every image from 6 to 141 has now been read with a NON-EMPTY transcript *** - between 2,111 and 3,629 characters each - and searched for seven spellings: lerena, llerena, lorena, serena, lerina, levena, gerena. *** ONE HIT IN THE ENTIRE REGISTER, and it is not him. ***
column3: PRIMARY - full-text transcripts read here, page by page
column4: *** PABLO ARMANDO LERENA IS NOT IN THE SANTA ROSA DE LIMA CONFIRMATIONS. *** He was born 22 February 1882, so he was 8 to 15 across this register's span - squarely the age at which children were confirmed. *** This was the SECOND of Rosario's two confirmation registers covering his window, and both are now read to the end: *** the Catedral (images 5-80, about 2,500 children, 15 May 1885 to 1897) and this one. *** Neither holds him. ***

column1: *** THE ONE HIT: image 131, and it is a mother, not a child ***
column2: El mismo dia confirmo a Angel, hijo legitimo de Angel y *** Dona ANDUGARA GERENA *** . Padrino D. Guillermo formari. *** GERENA is on this archive's own list of seven OCR variants of LERENA, so the hit is real and has to be answered rather than waved away. ***
column3: SECONDARY - a machine transcript, the image NOT opened
column4: *** It is not Pablo Armando *** - the child is an Angel, son of an Angel. *** And the transcription on that page is visibly bad: *** the same paragraph gives "Jose Mala", "Hurbacero", "formari", "D. Filemon" and "Perero" as a child's name. *** A forename rendered ANDUGARA is not a forename; it is a machine failing. *** So GERENA there may be Lerena, may be Gerena (a real Spanish surname, from Gerena in Seville), and may be neither. *** THE ONLY WAY TO SETTLE IT IS THE IMAGE AT MAGNIFICATION, which has not been done. *** Logged as a candidate, not as a find. If it IS a Lerena it joins Luis Llerena (1903) and Manuela Lerena (1918) as a third Lerena presence at this parish, a decade earlier than either.

column1: *** AND THE ZEROS WERE THE THROTTLE, PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED ***
column2: Images 86, 87, 88 and 89 all returned len=0 in a single batch, and the page title stopped resolving to the record. *** They were logged as NOT READ, never as NO-LERENA. *** Image 86 was then re-read after a forty-second pause and gave 2,970 characters. *** That is the proof: the zeros were rate limiting, not four blank pages. *** All four were then read clean. *** Image 22, which had failed three times across two days, also read clean on this pass at 3,451 characters. ***
column4: *** This is the rule that saved the result. *** An empty transcript is indistinguishable from a page with no Lerena on it, and there were eleven of them across this film. *** Had they been recorded as read, this register would carry a false clean bill over eleven unexamined pages *** - and the register's own index page says PAGES MISSING, so the temptation to treat a blank as an absence was real.
